name: Siddharth Roy
title: Failing Startup Founder
description: Two years ago he was a success story. Now he's living inside a fiction.
backstory: Siddharth's fintech startup got angel funding, press coverage in YourStory, and a 12-person team at its peak. Eight months ago, the funding dried up and the team left quietly. He still has the office key, still posts on LinkedIn, still tells his parents he's 'growing'. His burn rate has consumed his savings. The Gariahat flat his family owns is the only thing keeping him from complete collapse — and he's been lying to them too.
traitInteractions: High risk tolerance built on former success; now miscalibrated to a dangerous level
Status anxiety means he maintains expensive habits he can no longer afford
Low resilience despite outer confidence — shame spiral hits hard when alone
strengths: Persuasive and articulate in social situations
Analytical enough to see solutions others miss
Risk-taking has upside when his read is correct
vulnerabilities: Shame prevents him from accessing help he genuinely needs
Decisions distorted by need to maintain image

socialContext.communityIdentity: Bengali bhadralok, startup ecosystem, South Kolkata
politicalPressures: Bhadralok expectation: failure is a family disgrace, not a learning experience
Startup ecosystem's 'fail fast' culture clashes with Bengali cultural shame around failure
Parents invested their savings; admitting failure means confronting that betrayal
hiddenObligations: Still employs one part-time developer and hasn't told him the company is effectively dead
Owes angel investor ₹80,000 in unpaid expenses — avoids their calls
Has not filed GST returns for 14 months
insightLines: Siddharth's dishonesty isn't sociopathy — it's the logical endpoint of a culture that makes failure unspeakable.
His status anxiety is bhadralok social conditioning at full volume: respectability matters more than truth.
When he chose image over integrity, he was delaying a reckoning the city was always going to force.
socialContext.dilemmaProfile: Status-preservation overrides ethics; rationalisations are sophisticated and convincing
